title: Completing the square
examples: How do I find the minimum point using this method?
Can you show me an example with a negative number?
What is the difference between this and just finding the vertex?

explain.say: Today we learn to complete the square for quadratics. This helps us rewrite equations into a specific form. We will learn the (x plus p) squared plus q form. This form is very useful for seeing the turning point clearly.

items: Rewrite quadratics to a specific form
Useful for seeing the turning point

explain.say: Let us look at the equation x squared plus six x plus ten. We want to put this into the (x plus p) squared plus q form. Remember to take half of the coefficient of x. Half of six is three, so p is negative three.

We write down the first two terms as part of a squared bracket. So we have x squared plus six x, which is part of (x plus three) squared. Now we must expand that bracket to see what is missing. (x plus three) squared equals x squared plus six x plus nine.

Our original equation had ten, but our bracket only accounts for nine. So we must subtract nine and add ten. The equation becomes (x plus three) squared plus one. This is the (x plus p) squared plus q form.
Because the squared part is always zero or positive, the minimum value of the equation is one. The turning point is at x negative three, and the minimum value is one. This is the vertex.

faq.q: What does the 'p' in (x plus p) squared mean?
faq.a: The value p is found by taking half of the coefficient of the x term. If the x term is negative, then p will be negative. You can also find this by looking at the middle term when you expand.
asks: What is the coefficient of x?

faq.q: If I get a negative number for q, what does that mean?
faq.a: It means the turning point is below the x axis. The minimum value is still determined by the squared term, but the y value will be negative. The graph goes below zero.
asks: Can the minimum value be negative?
Does the graph cross the x axis?

faq.q: How do I use this form to solve an equation?
faq.a: To solve it, you set the whole expression equal to zero. Then you just solve the resulting quadratic equation for x. You are finding the x-intercepts.
asks: How do I find the roots?
What do I do if I set it to zero?
Does this help me find the x-intercepts?

faq.q: Is this method only for finding the minimum point?
faq.a: No, it is a way to rewrite the entire quadratic expression. This rewritten form is useful for finding the turning point and for graphing the curve accurately.
asks: Is this only for turning points?
What else can I do with this form?

faq.q: What if the x squared term is missing?
faq.a: If the x squared term is missing, it means the coefficient is zero. The equation is not a standard quadratic, and this method does not apply directly. You would need a different technique.
asks: Does it work if there is no x squared?

facts: The standard form of a quadratic is ax squared plus bx plus c.
The form (x plus p) squared plus q is also called vertex form.
The value of q represents the minimum or maximum value of the function.
The x coordinate of the turning point is always negative p.

quiz.say: Rewrite x squared plus ten x plus twenty-one in the form (x plus p) squared plus q.
quiz.why: Half of ten is five, so we use (x plus five) squared. Expanding that gives x squared plus ten x plus twenty-five. Subtracting four gives the correct form.

wrong.1: This mistake happens because students incorrectly use the coefficient of x, ten, instead of half of it.
wrong.2: This mistake occurs because students forget to adjust the constant term correctly after completing the square.
wrong.3: This mistake is common because students assume the original equation is already in the required form.

quiz.say: What is the minimum value of the function y equals (x minus 2) squared plus 7?
quiz.why: Since the squared term is always zero or positive, the smallest value it can take is zero. Therefore, the minimum value is zero plus seven, which is seven.

wrong.0: This mistake confuses the x coordinate of the turning point with the minimum y value.
wrong.1: This mistake assumes the entire function must equal zero at its minimum point.
wrong.2: This mistake incorrectly identifies the turning point as a coordinate pair instead of just the minimum value.

quiz.say: If the turning point of a parabola is at (4, -5), what is the equation in (x plus p) squared plus q form?
quiz.why: The x coordinate tells us p is negative four, so we use (x minus four) squared. The y coordinate tells us q is negative five.

wrong.1: This mistake forgets to change the sign of the x coordinate when writing it into the (x plus p) form.
wrong.2: This mistake incorrectly uses the y coordinate as the value for q instead of the negative of it.
wrong.3: This mistake expands the form but fails to simplify the constant term correctly.
